cmad.notes: MMS CMAD found on the MMS Science Data Center (designated location (b)) as a full PDF plus 12 chapters, and registered as DOI 10.48322/vshd-sv21 (SPASE Document record spase://NASA/Document/MMS/CMAD, recommended citation 'Burch, J. L., et al. (2024)'). Version read: V2.2 (Revision 4), submitted 8 May 2026 to the FY2026 Senior Review, mission status as of 30 April 2026 — it post-dates the 2015 start of operations, so its front pages are current-team evidence. Expected: MMS is operational and NASA-funded. Chapter 1 front matter names the PI (Burch) and Project Scientist (Le) as signatories; each instrument chapter names its current lead Co-I / points of contact and an emeritus-leadership list. The DOI record's author list (39 names: Burch, Giles, then a near-alphabetical remainder) equals the union of the author lists of the MMS data-product DOIs cited in CMAD section 1.12.2.

instrument_coverage.notes: Roster from CMAD Chapter 1 Table 1-2 (Instrumentation/Data Acronyms and Providers), the LASP MMS team page's instrument lead list, and the SDC FIELDS page's subsystem list; they agree. SPASE has 13 Instrument records per spacecraft x 4 spacecraft = 52, found by listing Instrument/MMS/ in the SMWG clone and confirming each ObservatoryID points to Observatory/MMS/1-4, whose ObservatoryGroupID is Observatory/MMS (the processed record has no downward links). Every measurement instrument on the roster has a SPASE record: AFG and DFG share the single FGM record; MEC corresponds to the Ephemeris virtual instrument; DSP has its own record. Not counted as missing: CMAD Table 1-2 also lists three data processors (CIDP, the FIELDS CEB, the FPI IDPUs) and two merged data products (merged FGM, FSM), none of which is a separately led measurement instrument. The suites (FPI, EPD, FIELDS) have no suite-level Instrument records; their leads are recorded against the sensor records. The SPASE Instrument records' InformationURL https://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/mms/spacecraft/mms-instruments.html returns 404, and the mission landing page's instrument page (https://mms.gsfc.nasa.gov/instruments.html) lists instrument types only.

Paper selection confident for all 12 papers. The mission overview (Burch et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-015-0164-9) has 'Overview' in the title, names MMS, was published online May 2015 in the dedicated MMS volume (Space Science Reviews 199) within months of launch, has 1,254 Crossref citations, and is the citation the CMAD (sections 1.9.2-1.9.3) and the SPASE CMAD Document record give for the mission. Semantic Scholar returns the same four authors (its citation count of 13 looks like a split record). ADS/SciX could not be queried (no API token; the abstract page failed a TLS check). Each instrument paper is the one CMAD section 1.9.3 names as that instrument's citation; all are in Space Science Reviews 199, online 2014-2016.

Author-order detection: overview (n=4) not alphabetized — positions 1-3 Strong, 4 (Giles) Medium. FIELDS (n=34), SCM (30), SDP (21), ADP/DSP (20), EDI (24), ASPOC (9): not alphabetized — positions 1-3 taken. HPCA (n=29): sorted suffix of 15 from position 15, prefix 14 — prefix 1-3 taken. EPD/EIS (n=26): sorted suffix of 18 from position 9, prefix 8 — 1-3 taken. FEEPS (n=27): sorted suffix of 25 from position 3, prefix = 2 (Blake, Mauk) — Baker at position 3 is in the alphabetized tail and gets no position evidence from this paper. FPI (n=97): strict backward scan finds a sorted suffix of 32 from position 66; in practice positions 1-7 are a deliberate prefix followed by alphabetized blocks (8-16 and 17-97, with small ordering slips) — positions 1-3 (Pollock, Moore, Jacques) taken either way.

FGM paper (Russell et al. 2016, n=23) ambiguity: the strict backward scan finds no sorted suffix because four names were appended out of order at the end, but positions 2-19 are an 18-name alphabetical run. Treated as partially alphabetized with a one-author prefix (Russell); Anderson (2) and Baumjohann (3) get no position evidence and are excluded. Erring against position here, as the skill directs for near-sorted lists.

CMAD DOI author list (39 names) ambiguity: Burch and Giles are placed first, and the rest is near-alphabetical but a strict scan finds only a 4-name sorted suffix because of data-entry slips (Torkar before Torbert; a garbled Eichelberger/Le entry). Treated as a two-name prefix plus an alphabetized remainder, so position is not used for the remainder. Remainder members are included at Medium only because each is independently named as an author of MMS data-product DOIs listed in CMAD section 1.12.2 (several are also corroborated by the LASP team page or instrument papers). A reviewer could reasonably read the DOI author list as the CMAD's front-page authorship, which would make all 39 Strong.

authorship_scope: the CMAD is a mission-wide document, so every included CMAD co-author is scoped 'observatory' (broadest evidence wins). This lifts 25 instrument and sensor leads to observatory scope. Only people whose sole evidence is an instrument paper stay at 'instrument' (FPI, ASPOC papers) or 'component' (sensor papers within the FIELDS suite: SCM, SDP, ADP/DSP, EDI). Mission leadership, Science Working Group leads and SOC/TMT/burst-system leads are also 'observatory'. If downstream prefers instrument-level ordering for CMAD co-authors, this is the field to revisit.

Observatory-run depth rule: from the 11 instrument papers only positions 1-3 (or prefix 1-3) are taken. Positions 4-5 are listed individually as excluded instrument-team depth, except where the person earned inclusion independently (Burch FPI 4, Ergun and Lindqvist FIELDS 4-5, Granoff SDP 5, Bromund FGM 4 and Jeszenszky ASPOC 5 via CMAD authorship). Authors at position 6 and beyond (about 285 author slots across the 11 papers) are not listed individually unless another source named them.

LASP MMS team page (https://lasp.colorado.edu/galaxy/spaces/mms/pages/2326576/About+MMS): all leadership-block and Science Working Group entries are evaluated individually. The 81-name 'MMS Science Co-Is' roster is used as CoInvestigator evidence for candidates who qualify through another source. The other 46 roster members are listed as excluded (roster only) — reviewer should confirm this scoping. Not evaluated individually, because they hold no qualifying role for the MMS investigation: 49 'Science Team Members' (four of them are candidates via other sources), three Interdisciplinary Science team rosters (NASA-selected separately and not continued into the extended mission), and 18 mission-operations and flight-dynamics staff (the Mission Director is listed as excluded).

Single-PI mission structure: every MMS Instrument record (all 13 instruments x 4 spacecraft) lists Burch as PrincipalInvestigator. This is the mission PI repeated on each instrument record, so it is recorded as PrincipalInvestigator evidence, not InstrumentLead. MMS calls its instrument leads 'Lead Co-I'. Current Lead Co-Is are mapped to InstrumentLead, and former or emeritus Lead Co-Is to FormerPI, naming the instrument — reviewer should confirm this mapping.

Curator items — outdated Instrument-record Contacts: DES/DIS list Giles (FPI lead to 2020; now Gershman); EIS lists Mauk (EPD lead to 2019; now Cohen); FEEPS lists Blake (the CMAD now names Gabrielse and Turner as FEEPS contacts, and Fennell until 2023); FGM lists Russell as TeamLeader (lead to 2023; now Wei); SCM, SDP, ADP, EDI and DSP list only Torbert, while the subsystem leads are Le Contel (SCM), Lindqvist (SDP/EDP) and Ergun (ADP). The Instrument Descriptions still use pre-launch wording ('will measure', 'is being developed').

Blake is given InstrumentLead from the FEEPS Instrument record Description ('FEEPS development is led by Co-I J. B. Blake'); the 2026 CMAD does not name him, so the reviewer may prefer FormerPI or no lead role. Moore's ProjectScientist role is historical (Phase C-2019) and Giles's is too (2019-2023); Guan Le is the current Project Scientist. Torbert's DeputyPI role ran 2007-2022; Genestreti has held it since 2022.

Deceased: Klaus M. Torkar (per the CMAD ASPOC chapter; the LASP page says 'retired') and Alain Roux (per the LASP Co-I roster) are kept as included authors on the strength of their founding-era papers — curator decision.

SPASE CMAD Document record (spase://NASA/Document/MMS/CMAD) curator item: its PublicationInfo/Authors string has data-entry errors — 'Hans, Ulrich' appears as a separate author, 'Eichelberger, Hans UlrichLe, Guan' merges two authors, a comma instead of a semicolon joins Leinweber and Lindqvist, and Torkar precedes Torbert.

Pre-launch NASA Goddard team page (https://mms.gsfc.nasa.gov/team.html, which describes MMS as 'launching in March of 2015'): the project-management, engineering and safety entries are excluded as non-qualifying roles. Its Project Scientist entry (Moore) is used. A 2014 GSFC project organization chart (https://mms.gsfc.nasa.gov/documents/mms_orgchart_04-15-14.pdf) turned up in web search. It is a project-management and engineering chart whose science-leadership entries match the LASP team page, so it was not harvested separately.

The CMAD (section 1.9.3) also cites four papers on the spacecraft, mission operations, the instrument-suite data system and the burst-data strategy (10.1007/s11214-015-0220-5, 10.1007/s11214-014-0087-x, 10.1007/s11214-014-0128-5, 10.1007/s11214-015-0150-2). None is the mission description paper, so their author lists were not harvested.

Dataset-level author lists (CMAD section 1.12.2 and the FGM citation example in section 1.9.1) were used only to corroborate CMAD co-authors. They belong to the NumericalData records and were not harvested as a separate candidate source. Their union adds no names beyond the CMAD author list.
